preamble: The voiceless retroflex sibilant [ʂ] backs to the voiceless velar fricative [x] through retraction and loss of sibilance. It is visible as a living dialect cline in Pashto, where the letter ښ is [ʂ] in Kandahar but [x] in the north, and in deep time as the Indo-European ruki outcome that separates Indic (which keeps [ʂ]) from Slavic (which retracted it to [x]).

examples.note: The letter ښ keeps the retroflex sibilant [ʂ] in the conservative southern Kandahar dialect, but in the north it became [ç] or [x]; Yusufzai and Peshawar speech have [x], so the language name is Pashto in the south and Pakhto in the north.
After *r, *u, *k, *i the PIE *s became a retracted (retroflex) sibilant, which Slavic retracted further to the velar fricative *x; likewise *paršás > *pȏrxъ 'dust'. Sanskrit kept the retroflex ष [ʂ].
